policy: Fixed stack margins qualify development-toolchain code generation, not the minimum supported language/library API level. Older supported compilers may need larger stacks in debug builds. Only workspace entries are skipped by the MSRV workspace test command; development-toolchain workspace runs skip none by name, and the entries whose tests are ignored in debug builds run in release builds through tools/verify.py.

tests.reason: Cold document schema compilation and local validation on a 256 KiB thread stack; Rust 1.88 debug code generation exceeds this margin.

Prepares value contracts whose patterns nest to the default pattern_depth, and checks values against them, on a 256 KiB thread stack. Release builds need at most 96 KiB; unoptimized pattern compilation needs up to 1 MiB, so debug runs ignore it on every host and tools/verify.py runs it in release builds.

Checks the preserved 39 recursive shape workloads at the former depth boundary and one level beyond it on actual 192 KiB, 256 KiB and 1 MiB threads. The original evaluator uses heap frames and no public stack-size option. Debug runs ignore this build-specific qualification; tools/verify.py runs it in release builds.

Prepares the preserved annotation-walk workloads at the former boundary and one level beyond it on actual 192 KiB, 256 KiB and 512 KiB threads, with one fifth already used by the caller. No public stack-size option or projected-walk limit remains. Debug runs ignore this build-specific qualification; tools/verify.py runs it in release builds.
